meta.topic: Place Value: Hundreds, Tens and Ones
meta.title: Place Value: Hundreds, Tens and Ones
meta.description: A complete Grade 2 place value pack for 3-digit numbers: base-ten blocks, building numbers, expanded form, digit value and comparing with >, < and =. Includes a lesson plan, worksheet, quiz, homework, flashcards, rubric, editable slides and Word files, and answer keys.
meta.overview: Students learn that the three digits in a number such as 346 stand for hundreds, tens and ones. They read numbers shown with base-ten blocks, build numbers from hundreds, tens and ones, write numbers in expanded form, find the value of a digit, and compare 3-digit numbers by looking at the hundreds first, then the tens, then the ones. Every answer in the pack is calculated by the generator and checked automatically.
learning_objectives: Read and build 3-digit numbers shown as hundreds, tens and ones (with base-ten blocks and in words).
Write 3-digit numbers in expanded form and give the value of each digit.
Compare two 3-digit numbers using >, < and = by comparing hundreds, then tens, then ones.
how_to_use: Teach the lesson with the slides and the lesson plan (base-ten blocks or drawings help a lot).
Use the worksheet for guided and independent practice in class.
Give the quiz at the end of the lesson or the next day, and score it with the answer key and rubric.
Send the homework page home for extra practice, and use the flashcards for quick daily review.
meta.skills_practiced: Place value, base-ten reasoning, expanded form, comparing numbers, explaining thinking
activity_ideas: Place value race: roll three dice to make a 3-digit number, build it with blocks, then say it aloud.
Human number line: give students cards with 3-digit numbers and ask them to stand in order from least to greatest.
Greater or less: pairs each draw a card, read their numbers and decide who has the greater number.
meta.teacher_tips: Always say numbers in two ways: "three hundred forty-six" and "3 hundreds, 4 tens and 6 ones". Watch for numbers with a zero, such as 405, which students often write as 45.
meta.differentiation_notes: Support: let students use real or paper base-ten blocks and a place value chart for every question. Challenge: ask students to find all the 3-digit numbers they can make with the digits 2, 5 and 8, and put them in order.
meta.assessment_notes: The quiz checks every objective (20 points); the rubric describes four levels for reading numbers, expanded form and digit value, comparing numbers and explaining thinking.

vocabulary.definition: one of the symbols 0 to 9 we use to write numbers
the value a digit has because of where it is in a number
groups of one hundred; the first digit in a 3-digit number
groups of ten; the middle digit in a 3-digit number

materials: Base-ten blocks (or the paper blocks drawn on the worksheet)

stages.name: Warm-up
steps: Count aloud by tens from 10 to 100, then by hundreds from 100 to 900.
Ask: "How many tens make one hundred?" (10) and "How many ones make one ten?" (10).

stages.name: Presentation
steps: Show 346 with base-ten blocks: 3 flats, 4 rods and 6 cubes. Say it both ways: "three hundred forty-six" and "3 hundreds, 4 tens and 6 ones".
Write 346 in a place value chart, then write it in expanded form: 300 + 40 + 6.
Show how to compare 346 and 364: the hundreds are the same, so look at the tens. 4 tens is less than 6 tens, so 346 < 364. Use the crocodile mouth: it opens toward the greater number.

stages.name: Guided practice
steps: Do worksheet activities 1 and 2 together. Students build each number with blocks before they write it.
Pairs complete activity 3 (expanded form). Ask two pairs to explain one answer on the board.

stages.name: Independent practice
steps: Students complete activities 4 and 5 on their own.
Check in with students who write numbers with a zero (such as 405) and ask them to build the number with blocks.

stages.name: Wrap-up
steps: Flashcard review: hold up a vocabulary card and ask students to give an example with a 3-digit number.
Exit question: "In 507, what is the value of the 5? What does the 0 tell us?"

support: Use base-ten blocks and a place value chart for every question.
Start with numbers that have no zeros, then add numbers like 405 and 650.
challenge: Find all the 3-digit numbers you can make with the digits 2, 5 and 8, then order them from least to greatest.
Write a number in expanded form with the parts in a different order (6 + 300 + 40) and ask a partner to find the number.

lesson_plan.assessment: Use the quiz (20 points) at the end of the lesson or the next day. Score open answers with the rubric. A score of 16 or more shows the student is ready to move on to adding and subtracting within 1,000.

sections.title: Read the blocks
sections.instructions: A flat is 100, a rod is 10 and a cube is 1. Write the number the blocks show.

items.prompt: What number do the blocks show? ____
What number do the blocks show? ____
What number do the blocks show? ____
What number do the blocks show? ____
7 hundreds, 3 tens and 7 ones = ____
7 hundreds, 7 tens and 0 ones = ____
7 hundreds, 1 ten and 7 ones = ____
5 hundreds, 5 tens and 7 ones = ____
3 hundreds, 0 tens and 3 ones = ____
2 hundreds, 9 tens and 2 ones = ____

sections.title: Expanded form
sections.instructions: Write each number in expanded form. Example: 352 = 300 + 50 + 2

sections.title: What is the digit worth?
sections.instructions: Write the value of the digit.

items.prompt: What is the value of the 4 in 472?
What is the value of the 1 in 134?
What is the value of the 3 in 239?
What is the value of the 8 in 108?
What is the value of the 3 in 893?
What is the value of the 3 in 931?

sections.title: Compare the numbers
sections.instructions: Write >, < or = in the circle. Look at the hundreds first, then the tens, then the ones.

items.q: In the number 582, which digit is in the tens place?
Which number has 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 6 ones?
What does the 0 in 309 tell us?

sections.title: Digit value
sections.instructions: Write the value of the digit.

items.prompt: What is the value of the 2 in 726?
What is the value of the 8 in 983?
What is the value of the 1 in 105?
What is the value of the 6 in 567?

sections.title: Expanded form
sections.instructions: Write each number in expanded form.

items.prompt: 4 hundreds, 8 tens and 5 ones = ____
9 hundreds, 7 tens and 7 ones = ____
8 hundreds, 2 tens and 3 ones = ____
4 hundreds, 9 tens and 4 ones = ____

sections.title: Skip count
sections.instructions: Count by tens or hundreds. Write the missing number.

sections.title: Read the blocks
sections.instructions: Write the number the blocks show.

items.prompt: What number do the blocks show? ____
What number do the blocks show? ____
What number do the blocks show? ____

sections.title: Think and explain
sections.instructions: Write your answer on the lines.

items.q: Write a 3-digit number that has 6 in the tens place.
items.answer: Answers will vary. Any 3-digit number with 6 as the middle digit, such as 462 or 865.

items.q: Ana says 250 is greater than 205. Is she right? Explain how you know.
items.answer: Yes. Both numbers have 2 hundreds, but 250 has 5 tens and 205 has 0 tens, so 250 > 205.

criteria.name: Reading and building numbers
levels: Reads and builds every 3-digit number correctly, including numbers with zeros.
Reads and builds most numbers; one or two small mistakes.
Needs blocks or a chart to read and build most numbers.
Cannot yet read or build 3-digit numbers without help.

criteria.name: Expanded form and digit value
levels: Writes expanded form and digit values correctly every time.
Mostly correct; may mix up the value of one digit.
Often writes the digit instead of its value (4 instead of 40).
Does not yet connect a digit's place with its value.

criteria.name: Comparing numbers
levels: Compares all numbers correctly and uses >, < and = correctly.
Compares most numbers correctly; may reverse a sign once.
Compares when the hundreds are different, but not when they are the same.

criteria.name: Explaining thinking
levels: Explains clearly using the words hundreds, tens and ones.
Explains with some place value words.
Gives an answer with a very short or unclear reason.
Gives an answer with no reason.

slides.title: Comparing numbers
bullets: If they are the same, look at the tens, then the ones.
